title: Advanced Broken Plurals
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 7; Ryding Ch. 7)
objectives: Recognize quadriliteral broken plural patterns (فَعَالِلُ and فَعَالِيلُ).
Identify additional triliteral plural patterns (فُعَلَاءُ, أَفْعِلَاءُ, فَوَاعِلُ).
Distinguish diptote broken plurals (no tanwīn) from triptote broken plurals.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 6: What grammatical gender and number does a predicate take when its subject is a non-human broken plural?

sections.heading: Quadriliteral & Diptote Broken Plurals
sections.body: Nouns with four consonants (either four-letter roots or triliteral roots with a prefix like مَـ) form broken plurals on the patterns فَعَالِلُ (with a short vowel after the long ā) or فَعَالِيلُ (with a long ī after the long ā). These patterns—along with فُعَلَاءُ and أَفْعِلَاءُ—are diptotes: they never take tanwīn.

sections.label: No Tanwīn on Ultimate Plurals
sections.summary: Broken plurals with two letters after alif (مَفَاعِلُ, فَوَاعِلُ) or three letters with medial yāʾ (مَفَاعِيلُ) are diptotes: they end in single ḍammah (-u) in the nominative and single fatḥah (-a) when indefinite.

sections.translation: The scholars are friends of the truth.
sections.irab: العُلَمَاءُ: مُبْتَدَأٌ مَرْفُوعٌ | أَصْدِقَاءُ: خَبَرٌ مَرْفُوعٌ (مُضَافٌ) | الحَقِّ: مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ مَجْرُورٌ
sections.notes: Both العُلَمَاءُ and أَصْدِقَاءُ are broken plurals of rational human beings, and أَصْدِقَاءُ takes a single ḍammah (no tanwīn).

sections.heading: Human vs. Non-Human Plurals
sections.body: Unlike non-human plurals (treated as feminine singular), broken plurals of rational human beings (like عُلَمَاءُ 'scholars') take plural agreement.
